THE BIG STORY
Mortgage rates dip

lines.text: Mortgage rates finally fell, for the first time since August.
lines.say: Mortgage rates finally fell, for the first time since August.

lines.text: On Thursday, Freddie Mac said the average 30-year fixed rate dipped to 7.32%.
lines.say: On Thursday, Freddie Mac said the average thirty-year fixed rate dipped to seven point three two percent.

lines.text: In early September it was 6.71%, then it climbed almost every week.
lines.say: In early September it was six point seven one percent, then it climbed almost every week.

lines.text: The week before, it was 7.40%, the highest in nearly three years, says the AP.
lines.say: The week before, it was seven point four percent, the highest in nearly three years, says the A P.

lines.text: And a year ago, the average was just 6.19%.
lines.say: And a year ago, the average was just six point one nine percent.

lines.text: For example, on a $400,000 loan, today's rate costs $301 more a month than last year's.
lines.say: For example, on a four hundred thousand dollar loan, today's rate costs three hundred one dollars more a month than last year's.

lines.text: Why the dip? Mortgage rates follow the 10-year Treasury yield, and the AP says it has eased lately.
lines.say: So why the dip? Mortgage rates follow the ten-year Treasury yield, and the A P says that yield has eased lately.

lines.text: Freddie Mac's next survey lands Thursday, right after the Fed meets.
lines.say: Freddie Mac's next survey lands Thursday, right after the Fed meets.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Mortgage rates finally fell. Here's what it costs you
post.ig:
Mortgage rates finally fell, for the first time since August.
Freddie Mac: the average 30-year fixed rate dipped to 7.32% on Oct 22, 2026, from 7.40%, which the AP called the highest in nearly three years.
A year ago it was 6.19%.
Example: on a $400,000 loan, principal and interest go from about $2,447 to $2,748 a month, $301 more.
Sources: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, AP, Bloomberg, Oct 22, 2026.
News and education, not financial advice.
